title: Cantar de mio Cid
titleEn: The Song of the Cid — The king summons a court at Toledo; the Cid's vigil at San Servando (tiradas 134–136, lines 2968–3059)
part: Tiradas 134–136 · The king summons a court at Toledo; the Cid's vigil at San Servando (lines 2968–3059)
source: Ramón Menéndez Pidal (ed.), Poema de mio Cid, 2.ª edición corregida (Clásicos Castellanos 24; Madrid: Ediciones de “La Lectura”, 1923), pp. 311–316, lines 2968–3059 (tiradas 134–136). Text follows Pidal's critical text exactly, including its old accentuation and mixed spellings; Pidal's italics (his editorial restorations) are shown in [brackets], and a line he restores whole is flagged in its note. Line numbers are Pidal's. Pronunciation convention: reconstructed twelfth-century Castilian. Translations made fresh from the Old Spanish; Pidal's notes and vocabulary (1908–11) the lexical aids.

sentences.t:
Dizidle al Campeador, que en buen ora nasco,
que destas siet se[d]manas adóbes con s[o]s vassallos,
véngam a Toledo, éstol do de plaz[d]o.
sentences.l:
Tell-him to-the Campeador, who in good hour was-born,
that of-these seven weeks he-make-himself-ready with his vassals,
let-him-come-to-me to Toledo, this-to-him I-give as term.
sentences.i: Tell the Campeador, who was born in a good hour, to make ready with his vassals within these seven weeks and come to me at Toledo: this I give him as his term.
sentences.n: Tirada 134 (assonance á-o) — the king summons a court at Toledo (Pidal: El rey convoca corte en Toledo). The line-ends run nasco, vassallos, plaz[d]o, fago, espaçio, ondrados, tornado, cuydado, Castellano … mandado: stressed á, then o; a new assonance, a new tirada, though the king's speech to Muño Gustioz runs straight on from the last part (no new opening quote: one per speech). Dizidle = decidle, 'tell him', the imperative with le glued on (d + l). que en buen ora nasco, 'who was born in a good hour', the en buen ora formula, with nasco, an old strong preterite of nasçer (= nació). destas siet se[d]manas, 'within these seven weeks' (sedmana = semana, the d Pidal's). adóbes = adóbese, 'let him make himself ready' (adobar, 'to equip, prepare'), the se cut to s and glued on; a present subjunctive of command, as is véngam = véngame, 'let him come to me', the me cut to m. s[o]s = sus, the o Pidal's. éstol = esto le, 'this … to him'; do = doy, 'I give'; de plaz[d]o, 'as term, as the appointed time' (plazdo = plazo, the d Pidal's). The king has fixed the day.

sentences.i: It is for love of my Çid that I hold this court. Greet them all for me, and let them take comfort among themselves: from what has befallen them they shall yet come to great honour.”
sentences.n: Por amor de mio Çid, 'for the love of my Çid', for his sake. cort, 'court' (house: cort/cortes 'court', the most solemn of the king's assemblies; Pidal's note to 2963 in the last part). fago = hago, f- for h-. Saludádmelos = saludadme + los, 'greet them for me', two pronouns glued to the imperative. Pidal's note to v. 2972: 'espaçio, "solaz, consuelo" (comp. espaciarse, solazarse); entrellos aya espacio, "alégrense" (pues el rey promete reparar el agravio). Esta traducción es aceptada por Bertoni, pero D. Hinard tradujo "saluez-les-moi tous, mettant entre eux une certaine différence", explicación caprichosa que aceptaron Huntington, D'Ovidio y otros' — 'espaçio, "solace, comfort" (compare espaciarse, solazarse, "to take one's ease"); entrellos aya espacio, "let them rejoice" (for the king promises to redress the wrong). This rendering is accepted by Bertoni, but D. Hinard translated "greet them all for me, making a certain distinction among them", a fanciful explanation that Huntington, D'Ovidio and others accepted' (espacio without the cedilla the second time, as printed; his quotes single, ours double inside his). The rendering follows Pidal. entrellos = entre ellos; aya, 'let there be', subjunctive of aver. desto que les abino, 'from this that befell them' (abenir, 'to happen, befall'). aun, 'yet, still'. ondrados = honrados. The king's speech ends here.

sentences.t: Espidiós Muño Gustioz, a mio Çid es tornado.
sentences.l: Took-his-leave Muño Gustioz, to my Çid he-is returned.
sentences.i: Muño Gustioz took his leave and went back to my Çid.
sentences.n: Espidiós = espidió + se, 'took his leave' (espedirse = despedirse), the se cut to s and glued on. es tornado, 'is returned, has gone back': ser as the auxiliary of a verb of motion, as French il est retourné. The preterite and the perfect side by side: epic tense-mixing. Muño Gustioz, so in the English (house).

sentences.t:
Assi commo lo dixo, suyo era el cuydado:
non lo detiene por nada Alfons el Castellano,
sentences.l:
So as he-said-it, his was the care:
not it holds-back for anything Alfons the Castilian,
sentences.i: As he had said, so he took the charge upon himself: Alfonso the Castilian let nothing delay it,
sentences.n: Assi commo lo dixo, 'just as he had said it' (Assi unaccented, as printed; assí elsewhere). suyo era el cuydado, 'the care was his': the king himself sees to it. non lo detiene por nada, 'he does not hold it back for anything', no delay at all. Alfons el Castellano, 'Alfonso the Castilian': Alfonso VI, king of Castile and León, so named in the poem; Alfons in the Old Spanish, Alfonso in the English.

sentences.t:
enbía sus cartas pora León e a Santi Yaguo,
a los portogaleses e a gallizianos,
e a los de Carrión e a varones castellanos,
que cort fazie en Toledo aquel rey ondrado,
sentences.l:
he-sends his letters for León and to Santi Yaguo,
to the Portuguese and to Galicians,
and to those of Carrión and to barons Castilian,
that court was-making in Toledo that king honoured,
sentences.i: he sends his letters to León and to Santiago, to the Portuguese and the Galicians, to the men of Carrión and the Castilian lords, that the honoured king was holding court in Toledo,
sentences.n: enbía = envía, 'sends'. cartas, 'letters', the king's writs of summons. pora = para. Santi Yaguo, 'Santiago' (de Compostela) in the English (house, as at v. 2925). portogaleses, 'the Portuguese'; gallizianos, 'Galicians', without the article. los de Carrión, 'those of Carrión', the Infantes' kin and people. varones castellanos, 'Castilian lords' (varón, 'baron, man of rank'). que cort fazie, 'that he was holding court': fazie = hacía, imperfect in -ie. The verb that governs the summons is the sending of the letters: the letters say the court is being held.

sentences.t:
a cabo de siet se[d]manas que i f[o]ssen juntados;
qui non viniesse a la cort non se toviesse por s[o] vassallo.
sentences.l:
at end of seven weeks that there they-should-be assembled;
who not should-come to the court not himself should-hold for his vassal.
sentences.i: and that at the end of seven weeks they should be gathered there; whoever did not come to the court should no longer hold himself his vassal.
sentences.n: a cabo de, 'at the end of'. se[d]manas, the d Pidal's. i = allí, 'there'. f[o]ssen = fuesen, the o Pidal's; f[o]ssen juntados, 'should be assembled'. qui = quien, 'whoever'. toviesse = tuviese; non se toviesse por, 'should not hold himself as'. s[o] = su, the o Pidal's. Pidal's note to v. 2982: 'El vasallo tenía obligación de acudir al llamamiento del señor; comp. 2893. Por eso el rey de León decía al conde Fernán González "quel fuesse a cortes o quel dexasse el condado", según la Crónica General' — 'The vassal was bound to answer his lord's summons; compare 2893. That is why the king of León told Count Fernán González "to go to the court or give up the county", according to the Crónica General.' The king's own words at vv. 2993–94 say the same.

sentences.t:
Por todas sus tierras assi lo ivan penssando,
que non falliessen de lo que el rey avié mandado.
sentences.l:
Through all his lands so it they-were-minding,
that not they-should-fail of what the king had ordered.
sentences.i: Throughout all his lands they were minding it, so as not to fail in what the king had commanded.
sentences.n: Por todas sus tierras, 'through all his lands'. assi (unaccented, as printed) lo ivan penssando, 'so they were thinking of it': ir + gerund, the action going on; penssar here 'to give one's mind to, see to' a thing, as in penssar de, 'to set about'. Who is thinking is not said: the people of the kingdom, summoned. The sense is clear, the exact nuance of penssando less so. falliessen = faltasen, 'should fail' (fallir). avié = había, imperfect in -ié; avié mandado, 'had ordered'. The tirada ends.

sentences.i: Now it begins to weigh upon the Infantes of Carrión that the king is holding court in Toledo; they are afraid that my Çid the Campeador will come there.
sentences.n: Tirada 135 (assonance ó, ó-e) — the men of Carrión beg the king in vain to give up the court; the court gathers; the Çid comes last, and the king rides out to meet him (Pidal: Los de Carrión ruegan en vano al rey que desista de la corte.—Reúnese la corte.—El Cid llega el postrero. El rey sale a su encuentro). The line-ends run Carrión, cort, Campeador, son, Dios, vos, sabor, buscó, Alfons, Remond …, with sabidores, mejores, Ansuórez: stressed ó, sometimes with an e after it. Ya les va pesando, 'now it goes grieving them', ir + gerund for a feeling that grows: it begins to trouble them. a ifantes, the persons again after les, and without the article, as often. por que, 'because'. fazie, 'was holding', imperfect beside a present (tense-mixing). miedo han, 'they have fear'. i = allí, 'there'. verná = vendrá, 'will come', the old future of venir.

sentences.t:
Prenden so conssejo, assí parientes commo son,
ruegan al rey que los quite desta cort.
sentences.l:
They-take their counsel, so kinsmen as they-are,
they-beg to-the king that them he-excuse from-this court.
sentences.i: They take counsel together, all the kinsmen there are, and beg the king to let them off this court.
sentences.n: Prenden so conssejo, 'they take their counsel' (prender = tomar; so = su). Pidal's note to v. 2988: 'assi parientes commo son, "tantos parientes cuantos son", "todos ellos" comp. 3606, y léase acaso igual en 2996' — 'assi parientes commo son, "as many kinsmen as there are", "all of them"; compare 3606, and perhaps read the same in 2996' (assi unaccented in his note; the text prints assí). So 'kinsmen, as many as they are', the whole clan. ruegan, 'they beg'. que los quite desta cort, 'that he release them from this court' (quitar, 'to free, excuse'; desta = de esta).

sentences.i: The king said: “I will not do it, so may God save me! For my Çid the Campeador will come there, and you shall do right by him, for he has a grievance against you.
sentences.n: No lo feré, 'I will not do it' (feré = haré, f- for h-). sín salve Dios, 'so may God save me', an oath. As at v. 2960 (sín salve el Criador), sín is best read as sí + me ('so me'), the m written n before s; Pidal's own note to v. 3042, on the same oath, glosses it 'así me salve Dios', 'so may God save me', which bears this reading out. darlêdes, the split future: darle hedes, 'you will give him' (= le daréis), the h of hedes unwritten and the two words run together, marked by Pidal's circumflex (as lê, lâ, mê). dar derecho a, 'to do right by' (house). rencura, 'grievance'; ha de vos, 'he has against you'.

sentences.t:
Qui lo fer non quisiesse, o no irâ mi cort,
quite mio reyno, ca dél non he sabor.”
sentences.l:
Who it to-do not should-wish, or not to-go-to my court,
let-him-quit my kingdom, for of-him not I-have liking.”
sentences.i: Whoever will not do it, or will not come to my court, let him leave my kingdom, for I have no liking for him.”
sentences.n: Qui = quien, 'whoever'. lo fer, 'to do it' (fer, the short form of fazer). quisiesse = quisiese. o no irâ mi cort: irâ = ir + a, 'to go to', run together and marked by Pidal's circumflex; both infinitives hang on quisiesse, 'whoever would not do it, or (would) not go to my court'. quite mio reyno, 'let him quit my kingdom', a subjunctive of command. Pidal's note to v. 2994: 'dél non he sabor, literalmente, "no tengo deseo de él", "no gusto de él"' — 'literally, "I have no desire for him", "I take no pleasure in him".' he, 'I have' (= tengo), aver as a full verb. The king's speech ends.

sentences.t:
Ya lo vi[d]ieron que es a fer ifantes de Carrión,
prenden conssejo parientes commo son;
sentences.l:
Now it they-saw that it-is to do Infantes of Carrión,
they-take counsel kinsmen as they-are;
sentences.i: Now the Infantes of Carrión saw that it had to be done; they take counsel, all the kinsmen there are.
sentences.n: vi[d]ieron = vieron, 'they saw', the old strong preterite, the d Pidal's. lo … que es a fer, 'it … that it is to be done': es a fer, ser a + infinitive, 'must be done'; the lo announces the que-clause. prenden conssejo parientes commo son, 'they take counsel, kinsmen as they are': Pidal's note to v. 2988 suggests reading this line, too, as 'all the kinsmen there are'.

sentences.t:
el co[m]de don Garçía en estas nuevas f[o],
enemigo de mio Çid que mal siemprel buscó,
aqueste conssejó los ifantes de Carrión.
sentences.l:
the count don Garçía in these tidings was,
enemy of my Çid who harm always-him sought,
this-one counselled the Infantes of Carrión.
sentences.i: Count García took part in this business — my Çid's enemy, who always sought his harm; it was he who counselled the Infantes of Carrión.
sentences.n: co[m]de, the m Pidal's; el co[m]de don Garçía, 'Count García' (house), the Garci Ordóñez of v. 1345, the Çid's old enemy at court. Pidal's note to v. 2997: 'en estas nuevas fo, "tomó parte en este negocio"' — 'took part in this business': nuevas, 'news, tidings', here the affair itself. f[o] = fue, the o Pidal's. siemprel = siempre le, 'always … him', the le cut to l and glued on; mal … buscó, 'sought (his) harm'. aqueste, 'this one'. conssejó los ifantes, 'counselled the Infantes', the person as a direct object without a.

sentences.t:
Llegava el plaz[d]o, querien ir a la cort;
en los primeros va el buen rey don Alfons,
sentences.l:
Was-coming the term, they-wanted to-go to the court;
among the first goes the good king don Alfons,
sentences.i: The appointed day was drawing near, and they were minded to go to the court; among the first went the good King Alfonso,
sentences.n: Llegava el plaz[d]o, 'the term was arriving' (plazdo = plazo, the d Pidal's), the day fixed at v. 2970. querien = querían, 'they wanted, meant', imperfect in -ie; who 'they' are is left loose: those summoned. en los primeros, 'among the first'. va, present among imperfects (tense-mixing). don Alfons, 'King Alfonso'.

sentences.t:
el co[m]de don Anrric y el co[m]de don Remond,
—aqueste f[o] padre del buen enperador,—
el co[m]de don Fr[ó]ila y el co[m]de don Bi[rbó]n.
sentences.l:
the count don Anrric and the count don Remond,
—this-one was father of-the good emperor,—
the count don Fróila and the count don Birbón.
sentences.i: Count Enrique and Count Remond — he was father of the good emperor — Count Fróila and Count Birbón.
sentences.n: co[m]de, each time the m Pidal's. Four counts ride with the king. Anrric, 'Enrique' (Henry) in the English; the same count is don Arric at v. 3037. Remond, a Raymond; Pidal's dashes set off the poet's aside, aqueste f[o] padre del buen enperador, 'this one was the father of the good emperor' (f[o] = fue, the o Pidal's): the poem takes it that its hearers know which emperor; the notes here do not name him. Pidal's note to v. 3002: 'Sobre estos condes, v. p. 19' — 'On these counts, see p. 19' (of his introduction). Fr[ó]ila, the ó Pidal's; his note to v. 3004: 'Para el conde don Fruela, v. p. 19. Alvar Díaz, p. 23' — 'For Count Don Fruela, see p. 19. Alvar Díaz, p. 23': Fróila is the old spelling of the name he writes Fruela. Bi[rbó]n, the rbó Pidal's (how far his italic runs in this name is not quite certain on the scan); Birbón is left as it stands. Alvar Díaz, whom the same note points to, comes at v. 3008 (see there). The counts are named in the English as in the poem; who they were historically is left to Pidal's introduction, which is not part of this text.

sentences.t:
F[o]ron i de s[o] reyno otros muchos sabidores,
de toda Castiella todos los mejores.
sentences.l:
Were there of his kingdom others many learned-men,
of all Castiella all the best.
sentences.i: Many others from his kingdom were there, men learned in the law, and from all Castile all the best.
sentences.n: F[o]ron = fueron, the o Pidal's; s[o] = su, the o Pidal's. i = allí, 'there'. Pidal's note to v. 3005: 'sabidores, "peritos en derecho"; el nombre completo era "sabidor de derecho o del fuero de la tierra", "sabidor legista"' — 'sabidores, "experts in law"; the full name was "sabidor de derecho o del fuero de la tierra" ("one learned in the law or in the custom of the land"), "sabidor legista" ("a learned jurist").' The court is a court of law. sabidores and mejores end in ó-e. Castiella = Castilla.

sentences.t:
El co[m]de don Garçía, [el Crespo de Grañón],
e Alvar Díaz el que Oca mandó.
e A[n]su[o]r Gonçál[v]ez e Gonçal[v]o A[n]su[ó]rez.
sentences.l:
The count don Garçía, [the Curly-one of Grañón],
and Alvar Díaz the-one-who Oca ruled.
and A[n]su[o]r Gonçál[v]ez and Gonçal[v]o A[n]su[ó]rez.
sentences.i: Count García, the Curly-haired of Grañón, and Álvar Díaz, who held Oca in command, Asur González and Gonzalo Ansúrez,
sentences.n: Now the Çid's enemies, the Carrión party, gathered at the court. el co[m]de don Garçía, Count García again (v. 2997), the m Pidal's; [el Crespo de Grañón], 'the Curly-haired of Grañón', a nickname (crespo, 'curly') and a place, the whole phrase in Pidal's italic: his restoration. The next line, e Alvar Díaz el que Oca mandó, is wholly italic in Pidal: the whole line is his restoration, not in the manuscript, printed here in plain type (Alvar unaccented, Díaz accented, as printed). el que Oca mandó, 'he who ruled Oca' (mandar, 'to command, hold'); Pidal's note to v. 3004 refers Alvar Díaz to p. 23 of his introduction; Oca is not identified in the notes. Then A[n]su[o]r Gonçál[v]ez, the n, o and v Pidal's: 'Asur González' in the English (house, Pidal's form). Pidal's note: 'Asur González es el hermano de los infantes, charlatán y comedor, que aparece en los v. 2172, 3373 y 3672. Gonzalo Ansúrez, padre de los infantes, ilustre caballero leonés, hermano del conde Pedro Ansúrez, p. 23-24' — 'Asur González is the Infantes' brother, a boaster and a glutton, who appears at vv. 2172, 3373 and 3672. Gonzalo Ansúrez, the Infantes' father, a famous Leonese knight, brother of Count Pedro Ansúrez, pp. 23–24.' Gonçal[v]o A[n]su[ó]rez, the v, n and ó Pidal's: the father, 'Count Don Gonzalo' elsewhere (house), here named with his patronymic. Pidal numbers that note 3008, though by his margin labels the Asur González line is 3009: see the note to 3009b. Pidal ends the line with a full stop and begins the next with small e, as printed.

sentences.t:
e Per Ansuórez, sabet, allís açertó,
e Dí[a]go e Ferrando í son amos a dos,
e con ellos grand bando que aduxieron a la cort:
e[n]bair le cuydan a mio Cid el Campeador.
sentences.l:
and Per Ansuórez, know-ye, there-himself was-present,
and Dí[a]go and Ferrando there are both two,
and with them great faction that they-brought to the court:
to-maltreat him they-intend to my Cid the Campeador.
sentences.i: and Per Ansúrez too — know it — was there; and Diego and Fernando are there, both of them, and with them a great band they brought to the court: they mean to trample on my Çid the Campeador.
sentences.n: e Per Ansuórez, sabet, allís açertó is wholly italic in Pidal: his restoration, printed here in plain type. allís açertó = allí se açertó, 'happened to be there, was present there' (açertarse, 'to be present, find oneself'), the se cut to s and glued to allí. sabet = sabed, 'know (it)', the minstrel's word to his hearers. Per Ansuórez, 'Per Ansúrez' in the English: presumably the conde Pedro Ansúrez whom Pidal's note at v. 3009 names as Gonzalo's brother (so the Infantes' uncle), though the note does not tie him to this line. Numbering: Pidal's margin prints 3005 on F[o]ron and next 3010 on e Dí[a]go, with five lines between, one more than the numbers allow; the structural check gave the letter b to this line, and the letter is ours, not Pidal's. His footnotes on the page count otherwise — '3008' on the Asur González line (our 3009) and '3011' on enbair (our 3012). Both footnotes, and the labels 3015, 3020 and 3025 (printed 3250), would agree if neither wholly italic line (the Álvar Díaz line and this one) had a number, as Pidal leaves his other restored lines unnumbered, and the label 3010 stood one line too high (it would belong to e con ellos); on that count this is 3008b, the Álvar Díaz line 3007b, and the extra line at 3014b is Pidal's 3014. The question is open; the numbers here follow the margin as printed. Dí[a]go e Ferrando, 'Diego and Fernando' (house), the Infantes, the a Pidal's. í = allí, 'there'. amos a dos, 'both of them'. bando, 'faction, band of supporters'. aduxieron = trajeron, 'they brought', old strong preterite of aduzir. e[n]bair, the n Pidal's; his note (numbered 3011): 'enbair, "atropellar, maltratar"' — 'to trample on, ill-treat'. le … a mio Cid, the person said twice, by pronoun and by name. cuydan, 'they intend'. Cid, without the cedilla, as printed here.

sentences.t:
De todas partes allí juntados son.
Aun non era llegado èl que en buen ora naçió,
por que se tarda el rey non ha sabor.
sentences.l:
From all parts there assembled they-are.
Yet not was arrived he who in good hour was-born,
because he-himself delays the king not has pleasure.
sentences.i: From every side they are gathered there. But he who was born in a good hour had not yet come, and the king was displeased that he was so late.
sentences.n: Pidal indents this line, a fresh paragraph within the tirada. juntados son, 'are assembled' (ser + participle, a state). Aun non era llegado, 'had not yet arrived', ser as auxiliary of a verb of motion. èl que, 'he who', with the grave accent as printed; en buen ora naçió, the formula: 'who was born in a good hour'. por que se tarda, 'because he is late' (tardarse, 'to delay'), the clause first; el rey non ha sabor, 'the king has no pleasure (in it)', is displeased. Numbering: the margin labels 3010 and 3015 allow four lines between them where Pidal prints five; the structural check gives this line the letter b (3014b), which is ours, not Pidal's. Counted from Pidal's footnotes it would be his 3014 (see the note to 3009b).

sentences.t:
Al quinto día venido es mio Çid el Campeador;
Álvar Fáñez adelantel enbió,
que besasse las manos al rey so señor:
bien lo sopiesse que í serie essa noch.
sentences.l:
On-the fifth day come is my Çid the Campeador;
Álvar Fáñez ahead-him he-sent,
that he-should-kiss the hands to-the king his lord:
well it he-should-know that there he-would-be that night.
sentences.i: On the fifth day my Çid the Campeador arrived; he sent Álvar Fáñez on ahead to kiss the hands of the king his lord, and to let him know for certain that he would be there that night.
sentences.n: venido es, 'has come', ser as auxiliary of venir. Al quinto día, 'on the fifth day', of the gathering. adelantel = adelante le, 'ahead … him' (the le cut to l and glued on): 'he sent him on ahead'. Álvar Fáñez, so spelled here (house 'Minaya Álvar Fáñez'; Minaya is not said in this line). que besasse las manos al rey, 'that he should kiss the king's hands', the vassal's homage, done on the Çid's behalf. so señor, 'his lord'. bien lo sopiesse que, 'that he (the king) should know well that' (sopiesse = supiese; the lo announces the que-clause). í = allí; serie = sería, 'would be', the conditional in -ie. noch = noche.

sentences.i: When the king heard it, it gladdened his heart; with a great following the king rode out, and went to receive him who was born in a good hour.
sentences.n: [od]ió = oyó, 'heard', the od Pidal's (the old odir/oír). plógol = plógole, 'it pleased him', the old strong preterite of plazer, with the le cut to l and glued on; de coraçón, 'from the heart'. yentes = gentes, 'people', here his retinue. cavalgó, 'rode'. iva reçebir, 'went to receive', ir + bare infinitive. al que en buen ora naçió, the formula again, 'him who was born in a good hour', a for the person.

sentences.t:
Bien aguisado viene el Çid con todos los sos,
buenas conpañas que assí an tal señor.
sentences.l:
Well equipped comes the Çid with all the his,
good companies that so have such lord.
sentences.i: Well equipped the Çid comes, with all his men — fine companies, as befits men who have such a lord.
sentences.n: aguisado, 'equipped, arrayed' (aguisar, 'to prepare, fit out'). los sos, 'his (people)', the possessive as a noun. conpañas, 'companies, troops'. que assí an tal señor, 'who thus have such a lord': fine men under a fine lord, the reflection running both ways; an = han, aver 'to have'. The loose que makes the exact turn uncertain; the sense of praise is clear.

sentences.i: When the good King Alfonso had him in sight, my Çid the Campeador flung himself to the ground: he wished to humble himself and do honour to his lord.
sentences.n: lo ovo a ojo, 'had him in sight' (ovo, preterite of aver). firiós = firió + se, 'struck himself', i.e. threw himself (down) to the ground, from his horse, the se cut to s and glued on (ferir, 'to strike'). Pidal's margin prints the number of this line as 3250, a misprint for 3025. Pidal's note to v. 3026: 'biltar, "humillar"' — 'to humble' (the same word as abiltar, 'to debase', v. 2942 in the last part, here of a self-abasement freely made): biltar se quiere, 'he wishes to humble himself', the se standing between the infinitive and quiere. ondrar = honrar.

sentences.t:
Quando lo [vido] el rey, por nada non tardó;
“¡Par sant Esidr[e], verdad non será oy!
sentences.l:
When it [saw] the king, for anything not he-delayed;
“By saint Isidore, truth not it-will-be today!
sentences.i: When the king saw it, he did not delay a moment: “By Saint Isidore, that shall not be today!
sentences.n: [vido], 'saw', the whole word Pidal's restoration (vido, the old strong preterite of ver). por nada non tardó, 'he did not delay for anything', a double negative of the ordinary Old Spanish kind. Par = por, 'by', in oaths. Pidal's note to v. 3028: 'verdad non será oy, "no por cierto", manifestando oposición al intento de humillarse que tiene el Cid; compárese 979.—sant Esidre, Santo de la devoción del rey, v. 1342' — '"certainly not", showing opposition to the Cid's intention of humbling himself; compare 979.—Saint Isidore, the saint of the king's devotion, v. 1342.' Esidr[e], the e Pidal's; 'Saint Isidore' (house). The king will not let the Çid kneel to him.

sentences.t:
Cavalgad, Çid; si non, non avría de[n]d sabor;
saludar nos hemos d' alma e de coraçón.
sentences.l:
Mount, Çid; if not, not I-would-have of-it pleasure;
to-greet us we-will from soul and from heart.
sentences.i: Mount, Çid: otherwise I should take no pleasure in this; we will greet each other with all our soul and heart.
sentences.n: Cavalgad, 'mount, ride', the imperative. si non, 'if not, otherwise'. avría = habría, 'I would have', the conditional of aver; de[n]d = dende, 'of it, from it' (the n Pidal's); sabor, 'pleasure'. saludar nos hemos, the split future: saludar + nos + hemos (= nos saludaremos), 'we will greet each other'. Pidal's note to v. 3030: 'saludar, "besar", se entiende que es besar en la boca, como resulta del verso 3034 y como se dice en el 2040' — 'saludar, "to kiss": understood as a kiss on the mouth, as appears from verse 3034, and as is said at 2040.' d' alma e de coraçón, 'from the soul and from the heart'.

sentences.t:
De lo que a vos pesa a mí duele el coraçón;
Dios lo mande que por vos se ondre oy la cort!”
sentences.l:
Of what to you grieves to me aches the heart;
God it may-order that through you itself honour today the court!”
sentences.i: What grieves you makes my heart ache; God grant that through you the court be honoured today!”
sentences.n: De lo que a vos pesa, 'from that which grieves you'. a mí duele el coraçón, 'to me the heart aches', the dative of the person. Dios lo mande que, 'may God order it that', God grant; the lo announces the que-clause. se ondre, 'be honoured' (present subjunctive, reflexive passive). oy = hoy. The king's speech ends.

sentences.t:
—“Ámen”, dixo mio Çid, el [buen] Campeador;
besóle la mano e después le saludó;
sentences.l:
—“Amen”, said my Çid, the [good] Campeador;
he-kissed-to-him the hand and afterwards him greeted;
sentences.i: “Amen,” said my Çid, the good Campeador; he kissed his hand, and after that he greeted him with a kiss.
sentences.n: Ámen, accented on the first syllable as printed, the stress of the period. [buen], the whole word Pidal's restoration. besóle = besó + le, 'kissed … his (hand)', the le of the person. le saludó, 'greeted him': by Pidal's note to v. 3030, a kiss on the mouth, the king's 'we will greet each other'. The Çid kisses the hand as vassal, then the king's mouth as the king has asked.

sentences.t:
“Grado a Dios, quando vos veo, señor.
Omíllom a vos e al co[m]de do Remond
e al co[m]de don Arric e a quantos que i son;
Dios salve a nuestros amigos e a vos más, señor!
sentences.l:
“Thanks to God, when you I-see, lord.
I-bow-myself to you and to-the count do Remond
and to-the count don Arric and to as-many that there are;
God save to our friends and to you more, lord!
sentences.i: “Thanks be to God, now that I see you, my lord. I bow to you, and to Count Remond and to Count Enrique and to all who are here: God save our friends, and you most of all, my lord!
sentences.n: Grado a Dios, 'thanks to God' (grado, 'gratitude'). quando, 'when, now that'. Omíllom = omíllome, 'I bow myself', the me cut to m and glued on (omillarse a uno, 'to bow to, greet', house). do Remond, do for don, as printed. don Arric, the don Anrric of v. 3002, 'Enrique' in the English. a quantos que i son, 'to as many as are here', the que doubling quantos. Dios salve, 'God save' (present subjunctive, a wish). e a vos más, 'and you more', you above all.

sentences.t:
Mi mugier doña Ximena, —dueña es de pro,—
bésavos las manos, e mis fijas amas a dos,
desto que nos abino que vos pese, señor.”
sentences.l:
My wife doña Ximena, —lady she-is of worth,—
kisses-to-you the hands, and my daughters both two,
of-this that to-us befell that to-you it-may-grieve, lord.”
sentences.i: My wife Doña Ximena — she is a lady of worth — kisses your hands, and so do both my daughters, and they pray that what has befallen us may grieve you, my lord.”
sentences.n: doña Ximena, 'Doña Ximena' (house: Ximena, not Jimena). Pidal's dashes set off dueña es de pro, 'she is a lady of worth' (pro, 'worth, profit'; de pro, 'excellent'). bésavos = besa + vos, 'kisses (to) you', the pronoun glued on. amas a dos = ambas, 'both of them'. desto que nos abino, 'of this that befell us' (abenir). Pidal's note to v. 3041: 'bésavos la mano que vos pese, "os ruega que os pese", comp. 2907' — '"begs you that it may grieve you"; compare 2907' (la mano, singular, in his note; the text has las manos): to kiss the hands is the form of a petition, and que vos pese hangs on it. The Çid's speech ends.

sentences.t: Respondió el rey: “sí fago, sín salve Dios!”
sentences.l: Answered the king: “yes I-do, so-me may-save God!”
sentences.i: The king answered, “It grieves me indeed, so may God save me!”
sentences.n: Pidal's note to v. 3042: 'fazer, verbo vicario: "me pesa, así me salve Dios"' — 'fazer, a stand-in verb: "it grieves me, so may God save me"': sí fago, 'yes, I do', fago standing for the verb just used (pese, 'may it grieve'), as English 'I do'. sín salve Dios, the oath of v. 2990, which this note paraphrases 'así me salve Dios', 'so may God save me': its así me supports reading sín as sí + me. The tirada ends.

sentences.t:
Pora Toledo el rey tornada da;
essa noch mio Çid Tajo non quiso passar:
sentences.l:
Toward Toledo the king turning gives;
that night my Çid Tajo not would cross:
sentences.i: The king turns back toward Toledo; that night my Çid would not cross the Tajo:
sentences.n: Tirada 136 (assonance á) — the Çid does not enter Toledo; he keeps vigil at San Servando (Pidal: El Cid no entra en Toledo. Celebra vigilia en San Servando). The line-ends run da, passar, salve, cibdad, Serván, llegarán, logar, çibdad, yantar, veluntad …, man: stressed á (salve with an e after it). Pidal indents the first line. tornada da, 'gives a turning', turns back (tornada, 'return'). essa noch = esa noche. Tajo, so in the English (house; the river that runs round Toledo). non quiso passar, 'would not cross'. Pidal's colon leads into the Çid's words.

sentences.t:
“Merçed, ya rey, si el Criador vos salve!
Penssad, señor, de entrar a la cibdad,
e yo con los mios posaré a San Serván:
las mis compañas esta noche llegarán.
sentences.l:
“Mercy, O king, so the Creator you may-save!
Think, lord, of to-enter to the city,
and I with the mine will-lodge at San Serván:
the my companies this night will-arrive.
sentences.i: “Mercy, O king, so may the Creator save you! Go into the city, my lord, and I with my men will lodge at San Servando: my companies will arrive tonight.
sentences.n: Merçed heading a request, 'Mercy, O king' (house), a courteous 'by your leave'. ya rey, 'O king', ya the vocative particle. si el Criador vos salve, 'so may the Creator save you' (si unaccented as printed, for sí 'so'; house). Penssad de entrar, 'set about entering', penssar de + infinitive, here a polite imperative: 'go in'. cibdad = ciudad, without the cedilla here, çibdad at v. 3050, as printed. los mios, 'my (men)', mios unaccented as printed. posaré, 'I will lodge'. Pidal's note to v. 3047: 'San Serván es el castillo de San Servando, separado de Toledo por el río Tajo (v. 3044) y por el puente de Alcántara. Tres años después de reconquistar a Toledo Alfonso VI donó el castillo al abad de San Víctor de Marsella, año 1088. Los monjes marselleses ocupaban el monasterio del castillo cuando el Cid celebró allí su vigilia. El castillo fué destruido en 1109 por los almorávides y reedificado en 1113 por el arzobispo y el clero toledano' — 'San Serván is the castle of San Servando, separated from Toledo by the river Tajo (v. 3044) and by the bridge of Alcántara. Three years after retaking Toledo, Alfonso VI gave the castle to the abbot of Saint-Victor of Marseilles, in 1088. The Marseilles monks were occupying the castle's monastery when the Cid kept his vigil there. The castle was destroyed in 1109 by the Almoravids and rebuilt in 1113 by the archbishop and clergy of Toledo.' las mis compañas, article with possessive, 'my companies'; the Çid's men still on the road.

sentences.i: I will keep vigil in this holy place; tomorrow morning I will enter the city, and come to the court before the midday meal.”
sentences.n: Terné = tendré, 'I will hold', the old future of tener. Pidal's note to v. 3049: 'vigilia, vela que se hace pasando la noche en oración dentro de un lugar sagrado. Precedía a varios actos graves, por ejemplo, al armarse caballero, y era costumbre velar antes de la lid judicial; por eso los del Cid velan las armas antes del duelo, 3544. El que celebraba la vigilia iluminaba a su costa la iglesia, 3055, y permanecía toda la noche de rodillas o de pie. La vigilia acababa al amanecer, con los maitines, la misa y las ofrendas del que velaba, 3060-62' — 'vigilia, a watch kept by passing the night in prayer within a holy place. It went before various solemn acts, for example being made a knight, and it was the custom to keep vigil before a judicial combat; that is why the Cid's men keep watch over their arms before the duel, 3544. The one keeping vigil lit the church at his own cost, 3055, and stayed the whole night kneeling or standing. The vigil ended at dawn with matins, mass and the offerings of the one who had watched, 3060-62.' aqueste = este. cras, 'tomorrow' (Latin cras); cras mañana, 'tomorrow morning'. enantes de, 'before'. yantar, 'the midday meal' (the noun from yantar, 'to dine').

sentences.t: Dixo el rey: “plazme de veluntad.”
sentences.l: Said the king: “it-pleases-me with good-will.”
sentences.i: The king said, “That pleases me with all my heart.”
sentences.n: plazme = me plaze, 'it pleases me', the pronoun after the verb at the head of the clause. de veluntad = de voluntad, 'willingly, gladly'.

sentences.t:
El rey don Alfons a Toledo [va] entra[r],
mio Çid R[o]y Diaz en San[t] Serván posa[r].
sentences.l:
The king don Alfons to Toledo [goes] to-enter,
my Çid R[o]y Diaz in San[t] Serván to-lodge.
sentences.i: King Alfonso goes on to enter Toledo, and my Çid Ruy Díaz to lodge at San Servando.
sentences.n: Pidal indents the first line, a fresh paragraph. [va] entra[r], 'goes to enter', ir + bare infinitive: va is wholly Pidal's, and so is the r of entrar; the one va serves both lines, and posa[r], 'to lodge', the r Pidal's, hangs on it too. R[o]y Diaz, 'Ruy Díaz' (house), the o Pidal's, Diaz unaccented as printed. San[t] Serván, the t Pidal's: San Servando (see v. 3047).

sentences.i: He had candles made and set upon the altar; he is minded to keep watch in that holy place, praying to the Creator and speaking with him in private.
sentences.n: Mandó fazer candelas e poner, 'he ordered candles to be made and set', the infinitives with the sense of the passive; the vigil-keeper lit the church at his own cost (Pidal's note to v. 3049, which points to this line). sabor a de velar, 'he has a mind to keep watch': a = ha, 'he has', aver unwritten h; sabor, 'pleasure, desire'. santidad, 'holiness', here the holy place itself. al Criador rogando, 'praying to the Creator'. en poridad, 'in secret, privately' (poridad, 'secrecy').

sentences.t:
Entre Minaya e los buenos que í ha
acordados f[o]ron, quando vino la man.
sentences.l:
Between Minaya and the good-men that there there-are
ready they-were, when came the morning.
sentences.i: Minaya and the good men who were there with him were all ready when the morning came.
sentences.n: Pidal's note to vv. 3058-59: '"Tanto Minaya como los buenos que hay allí, ya estaban preparados cuando vino la mañana"; para acordados, v. 3551. D. Hinard, "ils furent avertis lorsque vint le matin". Bello parece creer que acordarse significa "juntarse" y siguen al crítico americano Adam y Bertoni (si riunirono allo spuntar del giorno)' — '"Both Minaya and the good men who are there were already prepared when the morning came"; for acordados, see v. 3551. D. Hinard: "they were informed when the morning came". Bello seems to think acordarse means "to gather", and Adam and Bertoni follow the American critic ("they gathered at the break of day")' (the note runs on to p. 317). The rendering follows Pidal; 'gathered' is the other reading he reports. Entre … e, 'both … and', as Entre yo e mio Çid at v. 2959. los buenos, 'the good men', the Çid's knights. í ha, 'there are' (= hay). f[o]ron = fueron, the o Pidal's. man = mañana, 'morning'. The tirada and the part end here; the next tirada opens with matins at dawn.
